title: Desktop Automation MCP coordinate profile
description: Versioned, verifiable coordinate map used by the server's resolve_coordinate_profile_point/check_coordinate_profile tools for canvas applications without UIA. NOTE: profile_id is a human-readable slug (not a UUID); rationale is in schema/README.md. NOTE: verification_points carry only expected_color ([r,g,b]) and stay inside the safe region selected by reference_region_name. NOTE: reference_image_hash is NOT THE IMAGE ITSELF but the SHA-256 digest of the policy-masked reference-region PNG; the image is never stored in the schema, example, or test (local privacy principle). NOTE: safe_regions names must be unique, rect/point fields must stay within window bounds, and created_at must not be in the future; these cross-field rules cannot be expressed in JSON Schema, so they are checked by src/desktop_automation_mcp/coordinate_profile.py.

profile_id.description: Human-readable profile identity (e.g. ruffle-800x600-v1). Not a UUID: profiles are a small number of operator-managed files; readability in error messages, file names, and logs is preferred over opaque uniqueness.

application.description: Application the profile belongs to (one file = one application; consistent with the policy.schema.json model).

process_path.description: Single full executable file path (consistent with the executable_path pattern in policy.schema.json: a SINGLE string, not a list).

app_version.description: Optional application version. NOTE: not every application reports version information (e.g. unversioned nightly builds); this field is therefore NOT REQUIRED, but when given it cannot be empty. For an application with unknown version, the profile is guarded by the size+hash gates.

window_size.description: Window size at which the profile was recorded (pixels). A window of a different size does not match the profile.

reference_region_name.description: Name of the single safe_regions entry from which reference_image_hash was produced. The name must occur exactly once in safe_regions; verification_points must stay inside this region. This keeps profile verification from silently capturing the whole window.

reference_image_hash.description: SHA-256 digest of the allowed, policy-masked PNG region selected by reference_region_name (hashlib.hexdigest canonical form: 64 lowercase hex digits). NOTE: only lowercase is accepted; the uppercase variant is rejected to prevent normalization errors. The image itself is never stored.

safe_regions.description: Operator-preapproved safe click areas (window-relative). At least one region is required: a region-less profile cannot resolve any coordinate.

name.description: Region name; must be UNIQUE within the profile (uniqueness is checked by the Python validator).

rect.description: [left, top, right, bottom], window-relative pixels; negative values are therefore invalid. A negative screen/monitor origin is handled separately in the P2 matrix. left<right, top<bottom must hold and the rect must stay within window bounds (checked by the Python validator).

description.description: Optional human-readable note (e.g. which UI element this region is).

verification_points.description: Profile validity canaries: whether these points still have the expected color in the live window verifies that the application was not updated / the theme did not change. At least one point is required.

point.description: [x, y], window-relative pixels; negative values are therefore invalid and the point must stay within window bounds (checked by the Python validator).

expected_color.description: [r, g, b], each channel 0-255. NOTE: exact match is required, there is NO tolerance (accepting near-colors would be a silent assumption about a different version/theme; a non-matching profile is rejected and the operator re-records it).

created_at.description: Moment the profile was recorded; ISO-8601 date-time with MANDATORY numeric UTC offset (same as the expires_at rule in policy.schema.json: bare 'Z'/offset-less not accepted). A past date is normal since a record is a retrospective observation; a FUTURE date is rejected (checked by the Python validator).
